senses.def: (derivative of ἀγγέλλω ‘to tell, to inform,’ 33.189) a person who makes an announcement
a supernatural being that attends upon or serves as a messenger of a superior supernatural entity
senses.comment: In many languages a term for ‘angels’ is borrowed from another dominant language, but in other instances a somewhat descriptive phrase may be employed. The most common expressions for the ‘angels of God’ are ‘messengers’ and ‘messengers from heaven.’ Sometimes these angels are called ‘spirit messengers’ and even ‘flying messengers.’ In some instances they have been called ‘the holy servants of God,’ but an expression such as ‘servants of God’ or even ‘messengers of God’ tends to overlap in meaning with expressions used to characterize the role and function of the prophets who were sent as messengers from God. In some languages a term for ‘angels’ is contrasted with that for ‘prophets’ by calling angels ‘messengers from heaven’ and prophets ‘messengers from God.’ The ‘angels of the Devil’ are often called ‘the Devil’s servants.’|One cannot avoid problems involved in the rendering of ‘angel’ merely by borrowing a term. In some instances such a borrowing may already exist in the language and with a different meaning. For example, in one instance 'angel' had already been borrowed but with a meaning of babies who died at childbirth or shortly thereafter.

senses.def: pertaining to being pure, with the implication of not being adulterated
to cause someone to become a prisoner of war
senses.comment: In Ephesians 4:8 αἰχμαλωσία ‘captivity’ (55.23) is added redundantly to αἰχμαλωτεύω due to Semitic usage. The combination of words simply means ‘to take many captives.’

senses.def: pertaining to being real and not imaginary
a person greeted in the Epistle to the Romans

senses.domain: Stances and Events Related to Stances
senses.def: to straighten up from a bent over position

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to the lack of mercy or the refusal to be merciful
senses.comment: The meaning of ἀνέλεος and ἀνελεήμων is often expressed in highly idiomatic ways, for example, ‘to refuse to look at,’ ‘to turn one’s back on,’ or ‘to refuse to hear a person’s cries for help.’

senses.subdomain: Opposite, Over Against, Across From, Offshore From
senses.def: a position directly opposite and implying some space between
senses.comment: This expression in Acts 20:15 may be rendered in a number of languages as ‘we arrived near Chios.’

senses.def: to declare that one will cause harm to someone, particularly if certain conditions are not met
senses.comment: Because of the implied reciprocity in ἀπειλέω and ἀπειλή, one may translate 1 Peter 2:23 as ‘when he suffered, he did not say he would make them suffer.’

senses.subdomain: Not Able To Be Known, Secret
senses.def: to cause something to remain unknown, with the implication of concealment and inaccessibility
senses.comment: The passive expression ‘concealed’ may be rendered in an active form as ‘God has kept people from knowing about this wisdom.’

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to not having failed to keep the law (of God)
to add condiments to food
senses.comment: In rendering Luke 14:34 it may be necessary to translate ἀρτυθήσεται as ‘to cause it to taste like salt again’ or ‘to cause it to taste right again.’

senses.def: pertaining to a state of safety and security, and hence free from danger
pertaining to being certain and thus completely believable
motion away from a reference point with emphasis upon the departure, but without implications as to any resulting state of separation or rupture
severe pain associated with torture and torment
to begin vegetative growth, with special emphasis upon the sprouting of leaves
senses.comment: The initial stages of growth, either of a plant as a whole or in the renewal of foliage after a winter or dry season, may be expressed in a number of ways, for example, ‘to become green again,’ ‘to show leaves,’ ‘to see leaves begin,’ or ‘when leaves unfold.’

senses.def: to produce fruit or seed (of plants)
possessing information about
the content of what is known
esoteric knowledge (primarily philosophical and religious), with the implication of its being heretical and contrary to the gospel
senses.comment: In 1 Timothy 6:20, ψευδωνύμου γνώσεως may be rendered as ‘that which is falsely called knowledge’ or ‘knowledge which people think is true but is really false.’

senses.def: coming to an understanding as the result of ability to experience and learn

senses.subdomain: Whom or What Spoken or Written About
senses.def: a reference to an entity which one cannot or does not wish to make explicit (in the NT only a reference to a man)
senses.comment: Though in many translations δεῖνα is translated as ‘certain,’ this can give a wrong impression since it would imply that the individual is known to the parties involved or has been identified by the context.

senses.def: to awaken completely from sleep
(similar in meaning to ταράσσω[b] ‘to cause acute distress,’ 25.244, but probably somewhat more emphatic) to be mentally disturbed and thus deeply troubled
marker of cause or reason, with focus upon instrumentality, either of objects or events
a marker of discourse content, whether direct or indirect
senses.comment: The marking of direct and indirect discourse varies greatly from language to language. In some instances there is no marker at all; in other cases one marker precedes and another follows. In still other instances a repetition of an expression of speaking occurs at the end of a quotation, whether direct or indirect. In a number of languages written usage differs appreciably from spoken usage, because intonation so often marks introduced discourse in the spoken form of a language.|In Romans 8:21 διότι appears to be simply a variant of ὅτι[a], 89.26)

senses.def: west (as the direction of the setting sun)
senses.comment: In most languages east and west are related to the rising or setting sun, although in some languages there may be some local geographical feature which serves as a marker of direction, for example, the location of a particular mountain, the ocean, or a river. For north, some languages employ ‘to the left of the rising sun,’ that is to say, the direction is oriented in terms of the left hand of a person facing toward the rising sun. Similarly, south would be ‘to the right of the rising sun.’

senses.def: to carry out a custom or tradition
glosses: to be in the habit of

senses.def: (derivative of ἐκδικέω[c] ‘to punish,’ 38.8) a person who punishes
to put or place something out of an area
to explain something, presumably by putting forward additional or different information
a Hebrew term meaning my God
senses.comment: For certain problems involved in rendering an expression such as ‘my God,’ see the discussion in 12.1.

senses.def: material used in the construction of buildings
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand ἐνδώμησις in the sense of ‘foundation’ (see ἐνδώμησις[b], 7.41).

senses.def: that on which a structure is built
senses.comment: In some languages it is possible to describe a typical foundation in ancient times as ‘large stones underneath the walls.’ In other languages, however, this may seem to be quite a meaningless type of expression, since foundations are only made secure by driving stakes deep into the ground. Therefore, it may be best to describe the function of a foundation by ‘what keeps the walls firm’ or ‘how the walls are made not to move’ or ‘what goes beneath the walls.’|A number of scholars, however, prefer to understand ἐνδώμησις in the context of Revelation 21:18 as the material of which the wall was made, rather than as the foundation of the wall (see ἐνδώμησις[a], 7.77).

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
senses.def: pertaining to an extremely short period of time between a previous state or event and a subsequent state or event
senses.comment: In a number of contexts there is the implication of unexpectedness, but this seems to be a derivative of the context as a whole and not a part of the meaning of the lexical items.

senses.def: to listen to someone, with the implication of heeding and responding to what is heard
glosses: to pay attention to what is said

senses.def: to greatly desire to do or have something
to strongly desire to have what belongs to someone else and/or to engage in an activity which is morally wrong
causing to come together to, toward, or at a particular location
(derivative of ἐπισυνάγομαι[b] ‘to gather at,’ 15.124) the gathering together of a group (in the active rather than in the passive sense of ἐπισυναγωγή[a], 15.126)
to ask for information
senses.comment: In a number of languages a term such as ἐρωτάω[a] or ἐπερωτάω[a] implies an introduction of direct discourse, so that in Luke 9:45, for example, it may be necessary to translate ‘they were afraid to ask him, What do you mean by what you said?’

senses.def: to ask for, usually with the implication of an underlying question

senses.subdomain: Be Eager, Be Earnest, In a Devoted Manner
senses.def: a state of zeal based upon a desire to be involved in some activity or state
senses.comment: An equivalent of ‘serve wholeheartedly’ (Ephesians 6:7) may be expressed in some languages as ‘serve because you really want to’ or ‘serve because that is what you really desire to do.’

senses.def: a person in the genealogy of Jesus
a major OT prophet
a city of Macedonia
the host of Paul and Silas in Thessalonica
a person who sends greetings in Romans 16:21
a circular or semicircular band of light, whether colored or not
senses.comment: In Revelation 4:3 and Revelation 10:1 (the only occurrences of ἶρις in the NT) the reference may be either to a rainbow or to a halo. The meaning of ‘rainbow’ may be expressed in some languages as ‘a bow of light’ or ‘a curve of light’ or even ‘a ribbon of light.’ The meaning of ‘halo’ is usually expressed as ‘a circle of light’ or ‘a wreath of light’ or ‘a band of light encircling,’ followed by the object which the band of light encircles.

senses.domain: Stances and Events Related to Stances
senses.def: to be in a seated position

senses.domain: Stances and Events Related to Stances
senses.def: to cause someone to sit or to be in a seated position
senses.comment: For καθίζω as part of an idiom in Ephesians 1:20, see 87.36.

senses.def: to remain for some time in a place, often with the implication of a settled situation

senses.subdomain: Assign to a Role or Function
senses.def: to assign to someone a position of authority over others
senses.comment: In view of the particular context of 1 Corinthians 6:4 it may be necessary to indicate more clearly what is involved in such a designation. One may therefore wish to translate as ‘are you going to take these matters to be settled by people who have no standing in the church?’

senses.subdomain: High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to cause to sit at the right hand) to seat at the right hand of someone as an expression of assigning special importance or high status to such an individual
glosses: to seat at the right side
to give a special place of honor to

senses.def: (literally: to know what is in the heart) one who knows what someone else thinks
glosses: one who knows the hearts of
one who knows what people think
senses.comment: In a number of languages one may render this phrase in Acts 1:24 as ‘Lord, you know what all people are thinking.’

senses.def: a place for the lodging of travellers
a room in a relatively large structure (possibly an inn; see 7.11), which could serve as a dining room

senses.subdomain: Opposite, Over Against, Across From, Offshore From
senses.def: a position over against an object or other position
(with the genitive) marking a participant whose viewpoint is relevant to an event
one who exchanges currency, either in terms of different types of currency or different values of the same currency
a peninsula on the southwest coast of Asia Minor

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: drunken behavior which is completely without moral restraint
senses.comment: In a number of languages it may be possible to translate κραιπάλη as ‘bad things people do when they are very drunk.’

senses.def: (derivative of κύριος[a] ‘Lord,’ 12.9) pertaining to the Lord
senses.comment: A strictly literal rendering of ‘the Lord’s Supper’ might simply mean ‘the supper which the Lord ate,’ implying that no one else participated. Therefore, it may be necessary in some languages to translate ‘the meal at which the Lord presided’ or ‘the meal which the Lord had for his disciples’ or ‘the meal which the Lord ate with his followers.’

senses.def: to cause something to become white
senses.comment: This statement in Revelation 7:14 may raise numerous difficulties for receptors, since blood would not be regarded as an instrument for making anything white. It may be necessary, therefore, to introduce a marginal note explaining the figurative language and suggesting the rendering ‘to make them pure.’

senses.def: a stand designed to hold a single lamp or a series of lamps
senses.comment: One may translate ‘lampstand’ as ‘something on which a lamp could be placed’ or ‘a place for putting lamps.’

senses.def: (derivative of μαρτυρέω[a] ‘to witness,’ 33.262) a person who witnesses
a person who has been deprived of life as the result of bearing witness to his beliefs
senses.comment: A strictly literal translation of the Greek expression in Revelation 17:6 (ἐκ τοῦ αἵματος τῶν μαρτύρων Ἰησοῦ ‘of the blood of the martyrs of Jesus’) is likely to result in considerable misunderstanding, for it could mean that these were individuals who had been martyred by Jesus rather than those who had been deprived of their lives because of their relationship to Jesus. It would be possible to render τῶν μαρτύρων Ἰησοῦ as ‘those who had been killed because they belonged to Jesus,’ but one should avoid any expression which would suggest slave ownership.

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Units of Time: Daybreak, Midday, Midnight, Late
senses.def: the midpoint of the night
senses.comment: In some languages μεσονύκτιον may be rendered as ‘when the night is half over’ or ‘when the night is cut in half.’

senses.subdomain: Markers for a Negative Response to Questions
senses.def: a marker of a somewhat more emphatic negative response
senses.comment: Some persons have argued that the occurrence of μήτι in John 4:29 is contradictory, since it would appear from the context that the individuals posing the question regarded Jesus as a possible Messiah. On the other hand, asking the question in this form would have certainly fit the circumstances in which there was strong opposition to anyone claiming that Jesus was the Messiah. This form of the question would have avoided an overt commitment, while at the same time indicating peoples evident interest and concern.

senses.def: a marker of emphasis, involving some degree of contrast and/or comparison
(derivative of μύλος[a] ‘mill,’ 7.68) pertaining to a stone mill for grinding grain
senses.comment: The translation of such adjectival forms depends upon specific contexts. There is, of course, no need to translate an adjectival form by a corresponding adjective in a receptor language, especially when a noun would be more appropriate.

senses.def: to go without food for a set time as a religious duty
wood as a substance
senses.comment: A number of languages make a clear distinction between wood as a substance used in artifacts and constructions and wood used for heating or cooking. A further distinction may be made between durable wood (not readily subject to rot or to the effects of termites and borers) and less durable and therefore relatively unsatisfactory wood.

senses.def: wood as a substance used to burn for heat
senses.comment: ξύλον in Luke 23:31 may also be interpreted as a live green tree (see 3.4). If one assumes that the meaning here is ‘firewood,’ then it may be necessary to translate ‘wood which has not had an opportunity to dry out’ or ‘wood which is still green’ or ‘… which is still wet with sap.’

senses.def: large perennial plant, usually having a woody central stem, called a trunk, with secondary branches growing from it
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand ξύλον in Luke 23:31 as ‘firewood.’ One may therefore translate the first part of this conditional sentence as ‘if they do these things to firewood which has recently been cut’ or ‘if they do these things to firewood which hasn’t dried out’ (see 3.61).|In Revelation 2:7 and Revelation 22:2 ξύλον τῆς ζωῆς ‘tree of life’ may cause certain complications if the passage is translated more or less literally ‘I will give him to eat of the tree of life.’ In some languages a literal rendering would mean ‘to gnaw on the tree of life,’ that is to say, to eat the wood or the bark. It may therefore be necessary to translate ‘to eat the fruit of the tree of life’ or ‘… the fruit from the tree that causes life’ or ‘… causes people to live.’

senses.def: a heavy stick used in fighting

senses.subdomain: Instruments Used in Binding and Fastening
senses.def: an instrument consisting of heavy blocks of wood through which the legs were placed and then securely fastened
senses.comment: Stocks were employed primarily as an instrument for imprisonment, but also as a means of punishment.

senses.subdomain: Instruments Used in Punishment and Execution
senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of ξύλον[a] ‘wood,’ 3.60) an instrument of execution
senses.comment: Outside the NT ξύλον[f] often refers to a gallows, but in the NT contexts speaking of capital punishment, the reference is to the cross on which Jesus was crucified.

senses.def: a state of complete health or soundness in all parts of the body
senses.comment: In some languages it may be possible to translate ὁλοκληρίαν as ‘very healthy’ or ‘all parts of his body are healthy’ or ‘… strong.’

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to be relatively angry
(derivative of εἰμί[c] ‘to exist,’ 13.69) that which exists as property and wealth
senses.comment: In most contexts in which οὐσία occurs in non-biblical Greek, the reference is to considerable possessions or wealth, and accordingly it would be appropriate in Luke 15:12 to speak of ‘estate.’

senses.def: pertaining to being in every respect certain
a marker of strong emphasis, indicating complete validation of what is said
to happen to be in a place
(derivative of πατήρ[c] ‘ancestor, forefather,’ 10.20) pertaining to one’s ancestors
to move in such a way as to encircle an object
to consume liquids, particularly water and wine
senses.comment: In a number of languages a clear distinction is made between drinking water and drinking alcoholic beverages. Still other terms may be employed in speaking of drinking soups or broths.

senses.subdomain: Events Involving Liquids and Dry Masses
senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of πίνω[a] ‘to drink,’ 23.34) the action of a material which soaks up a liquid
senses.comment: Instead of speaking about ‘the ground absorbing the rain’ or ‘… drinking up the rain,’ it is often more natural to describe the event as ‘the rain disappearing into the ground’ or ‘the rain flowing into the ground.’

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to drink a cup) to undergo a trying, difficult experience
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is not possible to use the phrase ‘to drink the cup,’ since this will almost inevitably refer to the drinking of a poison cup as a means of proving innocence in an ordeal. Even if one uses a literal rendering of the idiom ‘to drink the cup,’ it is usually necessary to have some explanation as to the significance of the idiom.

senses.def: doing or performing (highly generic for almost any type of activity)
a Christian who sent greetings in 2 Timothy 4:21
(derivative of προσκυνέω[a] ‘to worship,’ 53.56) one who worships
the tip or high point of a building
a four-wheeled carriage or wagon used for travel or the transportation of loads
senses.comment: The term ῥέδη occurs only in Revelation 18:13 in a list of products bought and sold by merchants.

senses.def: one of the judges of Israel
Simon Peter, one of the twelve apostles
Simon the Zealot, one of the twelve apostles
a brother of Jesus
Simon of Cyrene, who carried the cross of Jesus
the father of Judas Iscariot
a tanner in Joppa
a magician of Samaria
a leper
a Pharisee
pertaining to a receptor
a state of security and safety
senses.comment: For another interpretation of στηριγμός in 2 Peter 3:17, see 74.20.

senses.def: a state of firm, inner strength
senses.comment: For another interpretation of στηριγμός in 2 Peter 3:17, see 21.13.

senses.def: to join two persons in a marriage relationship

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: an assembled group of worshipers or members of such a group
senses.comment: In James 2:2 συναγωγή may indicate the place of gathering, rather than the assembled group (see συναγωγή[c], 7.20).|In translating James 2:2 it is possible to render the conditional clause as ‘if a person comes into your church’ or ‘… into your congregation.’

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: a congregation of Jews
senses.comment: Since the borrowed term ‘synagogue’ in receptor languages so frequently refers only to a building rather than to a congregation, it may be necessary in Acts 9:2 to say ‘he asked for letters of introduction to leaders of the synagogues’ or ‘… leaders of the congregations of Jews.’

senses.def: a building of assembly, associated with religious activity (normally a building in which Jewish worship took place and in which the Law was taught, but in James 2:2 a Christian assembly place)
senses.comment: It is also possible to interpret συναγωγή in James 2:2 as a reference to an assembly of believers rather than to a building (see 11.44).|It is important to distinguish clearly between συναγωγή[c] and ναός[a] (7.15) or ἱερός[b] (7.16). There were many synagogues, but only one Temple in Jerusalem, and it is not enough to speak of synagogues merely as ‘small temples.’ It is better either to borrow a term for synagogue or employ a descriptive equivalent such as ‘places where Jewish people worshiped God’ or ‘buildings for worshiping God.’|It is also important to distinguish in translating between a term for ‘synagogue’ and for ‘church,’ whether as a reference to the congregation or to the building.

senses.def: a state of mental distress, involving acute anxiety
to be able to reason and think properly and in a sane manner
glosses: to be in one’s right mind
senses.comment: The meaning of σωφρονέω[a] is often expressed idiomatically, for example, ‘to have right thoughts,’ ‘to have one’s head,’ ‘to have straight thoughts,’ or ‘to have thoughts that do not wander.’

senses.def: to have understanding about practical matters and thus be able to act sensibly
cardinal number, where there are four instances of a countable entity
senses.comment: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘from the four winds’ or ‘from the four directions’ is simply ‘from every direction.’ The Greek expression does not mean from only four specific directions, but rather from every direction.

senses.domain: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products
senses.comment: τράχηλος also occurs in the NT in certain idiomatic expressions, for example, ‘to fall on the neck of someone’ (Luke 15:20 and Acts 20:37) in the sense of ‘to embrace’ (34.64), and ‘to put down their necks’ (Romans 16:4) meaning ‘to risk their lives’ (21.8). It is rare indeed that one can translate such idioms literally, since ‘to fall on the neck of someone’ may readily suggest a murderous attack, and ‘to risk one’s neck’ may be simply meaningless, since the custom of beheading as a means of execution may be relatively unknown.

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to put down the neck) willingly and purposely to expose oneself to extreme danger and risk
senses.comment: In some instances one can translate this expression in Romans 16:4 as ‘who showed they were willing to die in order that I could live’ or ‘in order to help me continue to live, they almost died.’

senses.def: the state of being healthy, well (in contrast with sickness)
senses.comment: In a number of languages health is expressed only in terms of strength, for ‘to be well’ is ‘to be strong.’ In other languages, however, to be well or to be healthy is a negation of illness or sickness, so that in Mark 16:18 one may translate ‘they will place their hands on those who are sick and these people will become not sick.’

senses.def: (derivative of ὑγιής[b] ‘right, accurate,’ 72.14) to be correct in one’s views, with the implication of such a state being positively valued
to accept the presence of a person with friendliness
an apparition
senses.comment: Most languages have quite satisfactory terms for ‘ghosts’ or ‘apparitions,’ since the psychological phenomena associated with such appearances are apparently universal. In some languages the equivalent of ‘ghost’ is simply ‘shadow.’ In other instances it may be literally ‘breath.’ In some instances the meaning of ‘ghost’ is incorporated within a verb expression, for example, ‘they saw, as it were, through him.’|The NT contains a number of lexical items (12.43-12.47) referring to supernatural powers believed to be active as elemental spirits exercising control over man’s fate. Though these may have certain special features associated with them and though in extrabiblical literature they may represent various grades of supernatural power, there seems to be no way in which they can be clearly distinguished on the basis of their NT usage. Appropriate equivalent expressions in other languages are extremely difficult to find, primarily because other religious systems usually have completely different beliefs relative to supernatural powers. In many languages it is simply not possible to speak of such supernatural powers without in some way identifying them with various kinds of spirits.

senses.def: to put something over or around the mouths of animals so as to prevent them from eating
senses.comment: In some languages it may be necessary to employ some type of descriptive equivalent of ‘to muzzle,’ for example, ‘do not tie the mouth of the ox so that it cannot eat’ or ‘do not cover the mouth of the ox so that it cannot eat.’

senses.def: to cause someone to have nothing to say
to cause to cease to make a sound
to have nothing to say, with the implication of being prevented from speaking (compare φιμός ‘muzzle,’ not occurring in the NT)
any light-producing object in the sky, such as the sun, moon, and other planets and stars
senses.comment: Though φωστήρ[a] may refer to any light-producing object, it is used especially of the heavenly bodies and more specifically of stars, as in Philippians 2:15, the one NT context in which φωστήρ[a] occurs. A focal component of this meaning is the light-giving characteristic.

senses.def: the state of brightness or shining
senses.comment: In a number of languages a clear distinction is made between some object which is bright in and of itself (that is to say, the source of brightness or radiance) and objects which are bright because they reflect light from some source. In the case of Matthew 17:5 (which is generally regarded as a reference to the Shekinah presence of God), the cloud would not be merely reflecting light but would be a source of light (see 14.50).

senses.def: patterned rhythmic movements of the whole and/or parts of the body, normally to the accompaniment of music
senses.comment: In a number of languages there are highly specific terms for various types of dancing, and one must make certain that the appropriate expression is used. Some terms for dancing may refer only to erotic dances; others, to highly ritualized performances in drama or religious practice; and still others may refer to personal expressions of happiness, joy, or grief. Special care must be exercised in selecting a term which will fit the context.

senses.def: a small piece of food (normally bread)
senses.comment: In Matthew 15:27, Mark 7:28, and Luke 16:21 (apparatus) the reference is to small crumbs or pieces of food that might fall from the table. In some languages an equivalent is ‘a small bit of food’ or ‘a tiny bite of food.’|This word is found as a variant reading only: ἐπιθυμῶν χορτασθῆναι ἀπὸ τῶν ψιχίων τῶν πιπτόντων ἀπὸ τῆς τραπέζης ‘being glad to eat the scraps that fall from the table’ Luke 16:21 (apparatus).
